glosses: Sediment or rock that is not native to its present location or is different from the surrounding material. Sometimes refers to ore or gems.

examples.text: Newly discovered oil and gas deposits at Nan-ch'ung in Szechwan also promise to be of increasing importance.

glosses: Bailment of personal property to be kept gratuitously for the bailor (depositor) and without any benefit to the bailee (depositary), e.g. for storage, carriage, repair, etc.
Money placed in a bank account, as for safekeeping or to earn interest.
Anything left behind on a surface.

examples.text: a mineral deposit
a deposit of seaweed on the shore
a deposit of jam on my countertop

glosses: A sum of money or other asset given as an initial payment, to show good faith, or to reserve something for purchase.

examples.text: They put down a deposit on the apartment.

glosses: A sum of money given as a security for a borrowed item, which will be given back when the item is returned, e.g. a bottle deposit or can deposit
A place of deposit; a depository.
To lay down; to place; to put.

examples.text: A crocodile deposits her eggs in the sand.
The waters deposited a rich alluvium.
This fear is deposited in conscience.

The lights of Luluabourg disappeared, and we were in the blackness of the African night, which was continuously pierced by the showers of red sparks ejected skywards and red hot ashes deposited on the track as the fireman rocked his fire.

glosses: To lay up or away for safekeeping; to put up; to store.

examples.text: to deposit goods in a warehouse

glosses: To entrust one's assets to the care of another. Sometimes done as collateral.
To put money or funds into an account.

examples.text: I had to deposit two months' rent into my landlord's account before he gave me the keys.

glosses: To lay aside; to rid oneself of.

examples.text: reform and deposit his error

glosses: To insult, belittle, or demean.

examples.text: They frequently put down their little sister for walking slowly.
People try to put us down / Just because we get around.

glosses: To pay.

examples.text: We put down a $1,000 deposit.

glosses: To halt, eliminate, stop, or squelch, often by force.

examples.text: The government quickly put down the insurrection.

22 March 2012, Scott Tobias, AV Club The Hunger Gameshttp://www.avclub.com/articles/the-hunger-games,71293/
For the 75 years since a district rebellion was put down, The Games have existed as an assertion of the Capital’s power, a winner-take-all contest that touts heroism and sacrifice—participants are called “tributes”— while pitting the districts against each other.

When the Nexus first arrived in Andromeda and an uprising arose among the desperate crew, it was William Spender who convinced clan leader Nakmor Morda to put down the mutineers. By all accounts, it did not go well.

glosses: To euthanize (an animal).

examples.text: Rex was in so much pain, they had to put him down.

A couple walking in Kirkleatham Woods, Redcar, heard whimpering and found the terrier-type animal in a mound of earth at about midday. It was rushed to a vet but its injuries were so serious it had to be put down.

glosses: To execute (a person), especially extrajudicially.

examples.text: The only thing left to do before putting the plan into action was checking the barracks for stragglers, and putting them down. She placed the first three bombs, then crept to the final door and opened it.

glosses: To write (something).

examples.text: Put down the first thing you think of on this piece of paper.

I hope you don't mind
That I put down in words
How wonderful life is while you're in the world

glosses: To terminate a call on (a telephone); to hang up.

examples.text:
Ray eventually called at 7pm and took the school’s side. He sounded imperious and distant and made me even angrier.
I told him he sounded just like my father, and put the phone down on him.
Don't put the phone down. I want a quick word with him, too.

glosses: To add a name to a list.

examples.text: I've put myself down for the new Spanish conversation course.

glosses: To make prices, or taxes, lower.

examples.text: BP are putting petrol and diesel down in what could be the start of a price war.

glosses: To place a baby somewhere to sleep.

examples.text: I had just put Mary down when you rang. So now she's crying again.

glosses: To give something as a reason for something else.

examples.text: She put her long life down to daily meditation.

glosses: To land.

examples.text: The pilot managed to put down in a nearby farm field.

glosses: To drop someone off, or let them out of a vehicle.

examples.text: The taxi put him down outside the hotel.

glosses: To cease, temporarily or permanently, reading (a book).

examples.text: I was unable to put down The Stand: it was that exciting.

glosses: To drink.

examples.text: I put down two bottles of red wine.
